newsitem.title: GERMANY: Troubled east German engineer to get state aid.
newsitem.headline: Troubled east German engineer to get state aid.

text.p: The east German development agency BvS and the state of Saxony on Wednesday offered help to troubled Chemnitz-based engineering group Heckert, which had earlier applied to be declared insolvent
"'Heckert will stay on the market' -- this is the message from the BvS and the state of Saxony to Heckert's customers and suppliers," the BvS said in a statement.
As soon as an administrator was appointed by the courts, negotiations could take place between the BvS, the state of Saxony and creditor banks, the BvS said.
It added that it expected the administrator to set up a rescue company, which would operate Heckert's activities during the negotiations.
With the cooperation of Deutsche Bank, which is the main creditor bank, Saxony and the BvS were ready to take part in discussions on the future of the company, the BvS said.
Heckert's managing director Peter Ulrich said earlier on Wednesday that the group had been unable to secure its liquidity.
Ulrich said production would continue and that the group had outstanding orders worth at least 50 million marks ($33 million). A quick solution had to be found soon, he added.
The company, which has 550 employees, has experienced difficulties since its parent company, Traub AG in Reichenbach/Fils, applied for protection from creditors.
